- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop sharply, missing the true mean-reversion trend.
- After a sharp price spike, model forecasts overshoot and fail to correct downward — overreacting to volatility.
- Model underestimates downward trends in later days of the 30d window, particularly when prices are falling.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, especially when historical mean is below 75.
- Model fails to adjust for recent downward momentum — ignores recent low prices in history when forecasting future values.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then become overly pessimistic in the last 10 days — exhibits “U-shaped” bias.
- Model does not account for seasonal or cyclical patterns — fails to recognize that prices often revert to prior 3–5 day averages after spikes.
- When true price drops below 70, model continues to forecast above 75 — exhibits “floor bias”.
- Model overfits to recent high prices, ignoring longer-term mean or trend — fails to recognize that prices often return to prior levels after short-term spikes.
